title: Secure your loose wrist-camera cable
instruction: The left wrist camera cable is hanging loose. Use the right hand to place the loose cable over the round retaining peg on the side of the left arm, then fold the upright hook-and-loop strap down over the cable and attach it to the round pad. Release the strap and move the right hand away.
context: A loose sensing cable on a robot needs to be routed and secured on the robot itself. This maintenance step restores cable management without a person handling the arm.
setup: A dual-arm YAM station with parallel grippers and its three original RGB cameras. Left arm starts at READY [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] rad; right initial joints and fixed base poses are in layout.json. A 740 mm long, 6 mm diameter, 120 g polymer-jacketed flexible camera cable joins a gray connector on the left upper arm to the mounted left wrist camera. Its free span hangs loose. A short polymer side-mounted retaining peg has a 40 mm long, 20 mm diameter shaft and a 40 mm diameter round end cap. A 140 mm long, 20 mm wide polymer-backed textile hook-and-loop strap (24 mm wide at the free end; 1.5 mm thick) stands in a curved open position above it. Its inner face attaches to the round cap. The wooden tabletop is1100×1300×60 mm, centre(0.36,0,0.7175) m and top z=0.7475 m. The gray proximal connector is24×14×24 mm and the mounted camera housing40×36×28 mm. The camera stand, floor and lighting are the pinned station primitives. No additional loose objects or layout randomization. Executable dimensions, mount pose and settled cable state are bundled.
scoring: Final-state score with continuous dwell:0.5 when the connected cable rests on the upper shaft behind the cap for1 s;0.75 when that cable routing remains and the strap inner face contacts the receiving pad for1 s;1.0 when both remain and the right hand is released (finger gap>80 mm), with its TCP>120 mm from the peg centre, for2 s. Otherwise0. Cable routing requires a centreline sample over the upper shaft, peg-local X in(-6,28) mm and radial distance13±2 mm from its axis (10 mm shaft radius plus3 mm cable radius), and a connected span crossing both sides of the shaft. Adjacent capsule endpoint gaps must remain below20 mm. Strap contact requires an inner-face segment centre within1.5 mm of the receiving plane and17 mm of its centre in that plane, facing inward within30 degrees. Ruler views and timed video measure the corresponding final placement and release.
reset_notes: Start a fresh simulator process for each trial. Cable and open strap are initialized from the supplied settled state before the first action. No object state is restored during the trial. Camera calibration remains fixed. For physical reset, peel the strap from the pad and restore its outward open bow; release the cable span to hang between its existing connectors as shown in the setup screenshot.
fidelity: Cable and open strap use articulated rigid segments with elastic joints and collision geometry. Hook-and-loop fastening uses an ideal local contact bond: an inward strap face must meet the receiving pad and sustain compression for0.2 s; only the engaged segment is attached, while the rest of the strap remains flexible.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0. Demo: 1420 steps / 71 s. Model: 1800 steps / 90 s.
